_comment: Two files of ONE npm package, declared a line each - the shape every vendored library really has, and the one that used to cost a request per file. The network map serves only the registry tarball: neither file URL is listed, so if the grouping stopped working they would 404 and both files would land in the untrusted family. Verifying against a package instead of against two URLs must change nothing a reviewer sees, so this expects no findings at all - the same empty report verified-vendor-source produces for its single file. The tarball publishes each file at the in-package path its declaration names (dist/...), because that path IS what the verification checks: bytes published elsewhere in the package are still a modified file.
